messages:
maria-ng: Heads up — noticed a sharp regression in tail latency and token/sec for mixed-arch pools ~30m after the CUDA/driver bump to 54888. Metrics: 99th+ latency +40%, overall throughput -12%. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/+/runtimes/perf

devon: saw it too. most traffic on the pool is hetero (A100 + older H100s). Autotuner returned different kernel choices after the driver change — favoring the vectorized-attn path for short sequences.

jonah: can you paste the autotuner telemetry? curious which kernel IDs flipped.

maria-ng: grabbing a snippet from the canary agent logs:

```
AUTOTUNE: model=gptx-16k, arch=A100, seq=32, selected_kernel=KV_VECT_7, score=0.87
AUTOTUNE: model=gptx-16k, arch=H100-1, seq=32, selected_kernel=KV_VEC_LEGACY, score=0.92
AUTOTUNE: post-driver: arch=A100, seq=64, selected_kernel=KV_VECT_9, score=0.65
AUTOTUNE: post-driver: arch=H100-1, seq=64, selected_kernel=KV_SLOWFALLBACK, score=0.44
```

maria-ng: also saw KV cache hitrate drop for sequences >48. Prefetching thrash increased.

lina: profiling traces show more expensive memcpy / synchronization on the H100 nodes when the vector kernel is picked. stacktrace attached in logs.

kyle: quick profiling top (hotspots):
```
90% nvlink memcpy (KV sync)
5% vector_attn_core
3% scheduler_queue_wait
2% other
```

devon: important detail: the heuristic that factors in `arch_score` was reweighted after the driver bump (driver exposes a different cuBLAS/cuda driver perf fingerprint). Autotuner interpreted that as "vector path is faster" on H100, but memcpy overhead kills tail.

jonah: agreed. two paths forward: 1) force a conservative fallback kernel on H100 for seq>=48 while we triage; 2) rollback driver on a small subset. Ops, can we canary rollback driver on one rack? @ops

ops: we can rollback on rack-3 (non-prod) immediately. Production racks require schedule window (2h). Can run canary in prod if you want but need approval.

maria-ng: let's do both: (A) pin kernel choice on H100 for seq>48 to `KV_STABLE_3` via runtime override config; (B) start rack-3 rollback to driver 54710 and run the usual perf smoke; (C) add a temporary autotuner safety net: require at least 3 continuous windows of improved latency before switching kernels after a driver upgrade.

lina: i'll put a conservative opt-in override in the runtime flags and push a canary rollout to 10% of H100 capacity. config snippet:
```
runtime.override_kernels: {
  arch_filter: "H100*",
  seq_gt: 48,
  force_kernel: "KV_STABLE_3",
  ttl: 1h
}
```

kyle: i'll wire a perf alert to lower the sampling window for KV cache hit histograms (so we can see improvements sooner).

jonah: if the rollback on rack-3 looks good, ops: schedule prod rollback for rack-5 and rack-7 during the 02:00 UTC window. Also we should add a short-term autotune blacklist for any kernel that increases memcpy time by >15% on the target arch.

ops: ack. starting rollback on rack-3 now, ETA 12m. will report back.

sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-274 — kernel-selection regression after driver 54888. Severity: P2. Assigned: eng-runtime. Links: https://inc.redwood/INC-274

maria-ng: thanks. after rollback/canary we should: 1) capture full nvprof traces for the vector kernels on H100, 2) run microbench for KV memcpy/kvcache prefetch interplay, 3) adjust autotuner scoring to include memcpy penalty. I'll own the scoring change.

devon: i'll take the rollback verification and perf dashboards. jonah, can you draft the autotuner safety belt change?

jonah: on it. will propose PR with gating heuristics and a blacklist threshold.

maria-ng: cool. if rollback shows improvement, we'll keep the runtime override until we ship a fixed autotuner and validated kernel. If rollback doesn't help, we'll escalate to Nvidia support (include traces).

ops: rollback done on rack-3 — preliminary metrics show 18% improvement in throughput and 25% drop in 99th on that rack. rolling back prod racks in the maintenance window.

devon: epic — thanks everyone. will update the incident and close the loop once autotuner PR lands. :tada:
